National transport: rail spur

The entire line requires 200 wood, 300 steel, 80 mechanical parts, 30 precision parts, 20 electronic components, and 40 tools. Once all materials arrive, two builders in Rail Town will work for 600 seconds. The existing reinforced truck will be kept as a backup vehicle.

Railway trains carry 128 per trip and take 45 seconds one way. They require 4 transport workers on permanent duty aboard, shared with relocation passenger service. Each departure costs an additional 2 coal, 0.1 parts, and 0.05 tools beyond the usual travel expenses to cover the round trip. If coal or spare parts run short, service stops until supplies arrive; trains will not run empty.

The reinforced truck still carries 128 per trip, takes 90 seconds one way, and requires 2 transport workers. Service can only be switched after vehicles in transit return to the station. Construction material delivery, mutual aid between the three stores, local relief, and routine trade all use the same vehicle on this line and the original stores at both ends.

Population, supplies, and responsibility ledger

The Eastern Plains stretch along both banks of the old canal, with broad fields, woodshops, and long flood-control levees. Medicine made in the North Shore, tools forged in the Eastern Plains, and public contributions sent to Old Town all require the three parties to negotiate and share the burden. Sending officials to survey the area is only to establish the facts, not to annex the land.
